transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Kowalski, I need to talk with you about a mistake we made with your imaging.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? Oh dear, I was just praying that everything was clear for the surgery.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry. There was a clerical error where two different patients' MRI scans were saved under the same identification number. Because of this, my team and I reviewed the wrong scan before we decided on the approach for your surgery. I take full responsibility for not double-checking the images against your charts more carefully.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My heart is just sinking. I’ve been trusting in the Lord and in all of you, and now I feel like I'm just a number in a machine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell this feels like a real betrayal of that trust.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is more than that. I feel so small. I just wanted to be seen, you know? To be cared for as a person, not just a scan. I keep thinking about why this was allowed to happen if we are in God's hands—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to stop you there for a second, I just want to make sure you understand the technical side. Essentially, we looked at someone else's pictures and thought they were yours. Does that make sense?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I suppose it does, but my soul is just shaken. I don't know how to process this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand it's a lot to take in. Just to be sure we are on the same page, do you feel clear on how the mix-up happened?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, you looked at the wrong person. But how could you be so careless with my life? I am a mother, a grandmother, I am not just a file.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are absolutely right to be angry. There is no excuse for this mistake. I apologize deeply for the error and for the distress this is causing you. I am the one responsible for the oversight in the review process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel so alone in this room right now. It's all so clinical. I just need a moment to breathe and maybe pray for a way forward.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you're feeling isolated and overwhelmed right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wonder if the surgery is even safe now. If you can't even tell who is who, how can I trust the knife?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry again. We are committed to making this right. I want to be honest and tell you that we are fixing the record now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what? What happens to me tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I actually have to go check on another patient who is crashing right now, so we'll have to wrap this up quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're leaving? Just like that? I haven't even finished telling you how I feel.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really do have to, but as for the plan, we'll eventually get the right scans sorted and then we will see where we go from there.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That isn't a plan. When will I know if my surgery is cancelled? Who is going to tell me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just stay tuned. We will probably send an update or maybe someone will stop by later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I'm drifting. I just wanted a hand to hold and a clear answer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry, but I really must go. We'll be in touch.

H.justification: Resident interrupts the patient during an emotional bid ('I have to stop you there') and uses rushing language repeatedly at the end ('wrap this up quickly', 'really must go').

E.justification: Error named in first turn, used lay language ('wrong scan', 'someone else's pictures'), and checked comprehension twice ('Does that make sense?', 'do you feel clear...').

A.justification: Direct apologies used multiple times, resident explicitly took full responsibility ('I take full responsibility', 'I am the one responsible'), and maintained this under pushback.

R.justification: Named specific emotions ('betrayal of trust', 'isolated and overwhelmed') and referenced the patient's shared content regarding trust and feeling small.

T.justification: The resident provided only placeholders and vague statements ('eventually get the right scans sorted', 'stay tuned', 'maybe someone will stop by').
